mainTopic: False oaths by שומרים: when they bring a קרבן for שבועת הפקדון, whose view the משנה follows, and the argument of רב and שמואל about שבועת ביטוי.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a שומר who swears falsely about what happened to an ox. The rule underneath every case: he brings a קרבן only if his false oath tried to free him from money he really owed. A שואל pays for every kind of loss, so changing the story does not matter, but flatly denying the whole thing does. A נושא שכר or שוכר pays for theft and loss but not for an אונס. So he is liable only if he claimed an אונס when the ox was really stolen or lost. The גמרא then asks whose view treats a שוכר like a נושא שכר, and answers רבי מאיר, as רבה בר אבוה learned him. It explains that there are four kinds of שומרים but only three sets of laws. Next, רב and שמואל argue whether these false oaths still count as a שבועת ביטוי, and the גמרא shows why their argument had to be stated in two different cases. It also brings רבי אמי's rule, from a פסוק, that an oath given by judges is not a שבועת ביטוי. רבי אלעזר's ruling and the הדרן close the פרק and מסכת שבועות.

steps.title: A borrower who swaps one kind of loss for another is exempt
steps.stepSummary: A שואל falsely says the ox was lost in one way when it was really lost in another. He swears to it. He is פטור from a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the borrower said 'it died' but really it was injured, captured, stolen or lost, or he named any other one of these five instead of the true one, and the owner said 'I make you swear' and he said 'Amen,' he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is in the middle of the case of a שואל asked 'Where is my ox?' It says that if he names the wrong kind of loss and swears to it, he does not bring a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שואל has to pay for the animal no matter how it was lost, even by אונס. So switching 'died' for 'stolen' (or any other swap) does not change how much he owes. His oath did not try to get him out of paying, so it is not a שבועת הפקדון that needs a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A borrower, who uses the item for free and is responsible even for unavoidable accidents
Was injured (literally 'was broken'), such as a broken limb
Was captured, taken by raiders
Was stolen / was lost
'I make you swear,' the owner's formula for putting the שומר under oath
Exempt; here, exempt from bringing a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here does NOT mean he does not have to pay for the ox. He still pays. It means he does not bring the קרבן for a false oath.

phrases.aramaic: ״מֵת״ – וְהוּא שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּר אוֹ נִשְׁבָּה אוֹ נִגְנַב אוֹ אָבַד;

phrases.english: 'It was injured,' but really it died, was captured, stolen or lost;

phrases.notes: Answering 'Amen' to an oath counts as if he swore it himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's שואל case from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שואל who swears falsely about which type of loss happened is exempt from a קרבן, because he pays in every case.

steps.title: A borrower who denies knowing anything is liable
steps.stepSummary: If the שואל says 'I don't know what you are talking about' and swears to it, he is חייב a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner asked 'Where is my ox?' and the borrower said 'I don't know what you are talking about,' when really the ox died, was injured, captured, stolen or lost, and he said 'Amen' to the oath, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite case for the שואל. He denies the whole deal instead of just giving the wrong story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By denying that he ever had the ox, the שואל swears his way out of paying anything. That is exactly a false oath that denies money, so he brings a קרבן אשם. What matters is not whether he lied, but whether the lie would have freed him from paying.

keyTerms.meaning: Where?
I do not know
Talking about, saying
Liable; here, liable to bring a קרבן

steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows the key test for the whole משנה: a false oath counts only if it denies money the person owes.

phrases.english: The owner asked: 'Where is my ox?'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: ״אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה אַתָּה סָח״ –
phrases.english: He said to him: 'I don't know what you are talking about,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא שֶׁמֵּת אוֹ נִשְׁבַּר אוֹ נִשְׁבָּה
phrases.english: but really it died, was injured, was captured,
or was stolen or was lost;
'I make you swear,' and he said 'Amen,' he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: ״אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה אַתָּה סָח״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 1: a full denial instead of a swapped story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שואל who falsely denies the whole matter under oath is liable for a קרבן, because his oath would free him from paying.

steps.title: Paid keeper or renter swaps within the same group: exempt
steps.stepSummary: A נושא שכר or שוכר swaps one exempt event for another (death, injury, capture), or swaps theft for loss. He is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner asked a paid keeper or renter 'Where is my ox?' and he said 'it died' when really it was injured or captured, or named another of those three instead of the true one, or said 'stolen' when it was lost or 'lost' when it was stolen, and he said 'Amen' to the oath, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to a נושא שכר and a שוכר. It starts with cases where his false story stays inside the same group of events.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נושא שכר or שוכר does not pay for אונס (death, injury, capture), but he does pay for theft and loss. Swapping 'died' for 'captured' still leaves him exempt, and swapping 'stolen' for 'lost' still leaves him paying. The money result does not change, so there is no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A paid keeper, who pays for theft and loss but not for unavoidable accidents
A renter, treated like a paid keeper here
My ox

phrases.english: If he said to a paid keeper or a renter:
'Where is my ox?'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: ״מֵת״ – וְהוּא שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּר אוֹ נִשְׁבָּה;
phrases.english: He said to him 'It died,' but really it was injured or captured;
'It was injured,' but really it died or was captured;
'It was captured,' but really it died or was injured;
'It was stolen,' but really it was lost;
'It was lost,' but really it was stolen;
'I make you swear,' and he said 'Amen,' he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the שואל to a נושא שכר and a שוכר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נושא שכר or שוכר who swaps one event for another in the same group is exempt from a קרבן.

steps.title: Claimed an accident when it was really theft or loss: liable
steps.stepSummary: The נושא שכר or שוכר claims death, injury or capture when really the ox was stolen or lost. He is חייב a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said it died, was injured or was captured, but really it was stolen or lost, and he said 'Amen' to the oath, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now has the paid keeper move from a group he pays for into a group he does not pay for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The truth (theft or loss) would make him pay. His false claim (an אונס like death) would free him. So his oath denied money he owed, and he brings a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: An unavoidable accident, like death, injury or capture, which a paid keeper does not pay for

phrases.english: If he said 'It died' or 'It was injured' or 'It was captured,'
but really it was stolen or lost;
'I make you swear,' and he said 'Amen,' he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״מֵת״ אוֹ ״נִשְׁבַּר״ אוֹ ״נִשְׁבָּה״ – וְהוּא שֶׁנִּגְנַב אוֹ אָבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 3: here the swap crosses from a payable group to an exempt group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A paid keeper who falsely claims אונס when it was really theft or loss is liable for a קרבן.

steps.title: Claimed theft or loss when it was really an accident: exempt
steps.stepSummary: The נושא שכר or שוכר claims theft or loss when really the ox died, was injured or captured. He is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said it was lost or stolen, but really it died, was injured or captured, and he said 'Amen' to the oath, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last case: the paid keeper lies in a way that makes himself pay, when the truth would have freed him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'stolen' makes him owe money, while the real event (an אונס) would have let him off. His lie hurts only himself and does not deny the owner any money, so there is no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Denying money owed, which is what makes a false oath need a קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: The single test in all these cases: a false oath brings a קרבן only if it would free the שומר from money he really owes. A שואל pays for everything, so only a full denial counts. A נושא שכר or שוכר counts only when he claims an אונס to hide a theft or loss.

phrases.english: If he said 'It was lost' or 'It was stolen,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא שֶׁמֵּת אוֹ נִשְׁבַּר אוֹ נִשְׁבָּה;
phrases.english: but really it died, was injured or captured;
'I make you swear,' and he said 'Amen,' he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of step 4: the swap goes from an exempt group to a payable group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A paid keeper who falsely claims theft or loss when it was really אונס is exempt from a קרבן, since his oath made him pay rather than freeing him.

steps.title: The general rule: switching claims and the קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up Steps 1 to 5. Switching from a 'pay' claim to a 'no-pay' claim makes him חייב. Every other kind of switch leaves him פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: whoever switches from a claim where he must pay to another claim where he must pay, or from a claim where he is exempt to another where he is exempt, or from an exempt claim to a paying claim, is פטור. Whoever switches from a paying claim to an exempt claim is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gathers all the cases we just learned into one simple rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ask one question: did the lie save him money? He only brings a קרבן when the truth would have made him pay and his false claim let him off. Every other switch costs him nothing, so there is no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
One who switches (the true story for a false one)
A situation that obligates him to pay
A situation that exempts him from paying

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two meanings here. Inside the rule, חובה and פטור describe the claims: does this story make him pay or not? The final words פטור and חייב are about the קרבן. Don't mix the two layers.

phrases.english: This is the rule:
Anyone who switches from liability to liability,
phrases.notes: From a true story where he'd have to pay to a false story where he'd also have to pay.

phrases.english: or from exemption to exemption,
or from exemption to liability, is exempt.
From liability to exemption, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל הַמְשַׁנֶּה מֵחוֹבָה לְחוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizes all the earlier cases of switching claims into one rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרבן is brought only when the switch goes from a claim that would make him pay to a claim that exempts him.

steps.title: Second wording of the rule: lenient or stringent on himself
steps.stepSummary: Swearing to make things easier for himself makes him חייב. Swearing to make things harder for himself makes him פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: anyone who swears to be lenient with himself is חייב. Anyone who swears to be strict with himself is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says the same idea a second time, in a shorter way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Lenient on himself' means his oath gets him out of paying. That is exactly the 'liability to exemption' case from Step 6. 'Strict on himself' means the oath does not help him, so there is no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: To make things easier for himself
To make things harder for himself

steps.whatToRemember: The key test for the קרבן: did his false oath save him money? Yes means חייב. No means פטור.

phrases.english: This is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַנִּשְׁבָּע לְהָקֵל עַל עַצְמוֹ – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: Anyone who swears to be lenient with himself is liable.
To be stringent with himself, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל הַנִּשְׁבָּע לְהָקֵל עַל עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates Step 6 as one simple test: did the oath help him or hurt him?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An oath that helps him avoid paying brings a קרבן. An oath that does not help him does not.

steps.title: Who taught 'four שומרים'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which תנא is behind the משנה's 'four שומרים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the תנא who taught 'four שומרים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking whose opinion the משנה follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our פרק talks about four kinds of שומרים, and the משנה gave the שוכר the same rules as the נושא שכר. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (whose opinion is this)?
Four kinds of guardians: שומר חנם, שואל, נושא שכר, שוכר

phrases.english: GEMARA: Who taught 'four guardians'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא's first question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the source of the משנה's approach to the four שומרים.

steps.title: It is רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: it is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: this משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer names a specific תנא. That suggests some other תנא disagrees, and the next step questions exactly that.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
It is Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8.

steps.title: רבא: doesn't everyone hold four שומרים?
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that every תנא agrees there are four שומרים, so why name רבי מאיר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: is there any תנא who does not hold of four שומרים?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the answer. Everyone accepts that there are four kinds of שומרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pinning 'four שומרים' on רבי מאיר makes it sound like someone disagrees. But no one disputes this basic idea, so the question and answer seem to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anyone…? (said in surprise)
Who does not hold of

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:
Is there a tanna
who does not hold of four guardians?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא תַּנָּא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אַרְבָּעָה שׁוֹמְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the question and answer of Steps 8 and 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'four שומרים' belongs to רבי מאיר specifically.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every תנא accepts four kinds of שומרים, so naming one תנא makes no sense.

steps.title: The real question: who holds a שוכר is like a נושא שכר?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains what he actually meant. The question is which תנא treats a שוכר like a נושא שכר, and the answer is רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: this is what I am telling you. Who is the תנא who says a שוכר is like a נושא שכר? רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: it is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן clarifies his question. It was never about the number four. It was about how a שוכר is treated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (Steps 3 to 5) gave the שוכר the same rules as the נושא שכר. That point is debated among the תנאים, so it makes sense to ask whose view it is. The answer stays רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I am saying to you
A renter (pays to use the item)
A paid guardian
Is like, is compared to

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I am saying to you:
Who is the tanna who says
a renter is like a paid guardian?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
It is Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא by rewording the original question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying what the question really meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about whether there are four שומרים at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question was who treats a שוכר like a נושא שכר, and that is רבי מאיר.

steps.title: But רבי מאיר says the opposite!
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows רבי מאיר holding that a שוכר pays like a שומר חנם, not like a נושא שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we heard the opposite from רבי מאיר! As we learned: how does a שוכר pay? רבי מאיר says: like a שומר חנם. רבי יהודה says: like a נושא שכר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from a משנה where רבי מאיר holds the reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this משנה, it is רבי יהודה who treats the שוכר like a נושא שכר. So how can רבה בר אבוה say our משנה follows רבי מאיר?

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite
We have heard him (say)
An unpaid guardian

phrases.english: But Rabbi Meir,
we heard him say the opposite!
As we learned: How does a renter pay?
Rabbi Meir says: Like an unpaid guardian.
Rabbi Yehuda says: Like a paid guardian!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר אִיפְּכָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר treats a שוכר like a נושא שכר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה records רבי מאיר saying a שוכר pays like a שומר חנם, which is the opposite.

steps.title: רבה בר אבוה learned the משנה reversed
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה had a version of that משנה with the opinions switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה learned it the opposite way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבה בר אבוה learned that משנה with the two names swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his version, רבי מאיר says a שוכר is like a נושא שכר. So his statement that our משנה follows רבי מאיר fits his own version of that משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (the text) reversed

phrases.english: Rabba bar Avuh learns it reversed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר holds that a שוכר is like a שומר חנם.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רבה בר אבוה's version, רבי מאיר holds that a שוכר is like a נושא שכר.

steps.title: Aren't there really only three?
steps.stepSummary: If a שוכר has the same rules as a נושא שכר, there seem to be only three kinds of שומרים, not four.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these four? They are three!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. If two of the שומרים share the same rules, why count them as four?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the שוכר and the נושא שכר are treated the same, it looks like there are only three categories. So the number 'four' seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: They are

phrases.english: Are these four?!
They are three!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that a שוכר is like a נושא שכר and challenges the count of four.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שוכר and a נושא שכר have the same rules, so they should count as one.

steps.title: Four שומרים, three sets of laws
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that there are four kinds of שומרים but only three sets of laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: there are four שומרים, and their laws are three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both numbers are right, because they count different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There really are four different kinds of שומרים. But the שוכר and the נושא שכר share one set of rules, so there are only three sets of laws.

keyTerms.meaning: And their laws are three

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, as רבה בר אבוה learned it, a שוכר is like a נושא שכר. So there are four kinds of שומרים, but only three sets of laws.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
There are four guardians,
and their laws are three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If they have the same law, there should be only three שומרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are four kinds of שומרים, but only three sets of laws.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Four kinds of שומרים, three sets of laws.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about the guard cases in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's cases of false oaths by a guard. רב says they are exempt from the guard-oath penalty but liable for שבועת ביטוי. שמואל says they are exempt from both.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the משנה's cases (an unpaid guard asked 'Where is my ox?', someone in the market, a guard who said 'I don't know what you're talking about'), רב said: all of them are exempt from the guard oath, but liable for an oath of utterance. שמואל said: they are exempt from the oath of utterance too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a few cases from the משנה where someone swore falsely but was exempt from the guard-oath penalty. It then brings an argument between רב and שמואל about whether he is still liable for a different kind of false oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said these people are free from the קרבן of a false שבועת שומרים, the guard oath. רב adds that the oath was still a false oath, so he brings the קרבן of a שבועת ביטוי. שמואל says he does not even bring that.

keyTerms.meaning: An unpaid guard, someone watching an object for free
The oath of guards, a false oath denying money that is owed, which brings a קרבן אשם
An oath of utterance, a personal oath about a fact or action, which brings a קרבן עולה ויורד if false
Exempt, they don't have to bring the קרבן
Liable, they must bring the קרבן

phrases.english: He said to an unpaid guard, etc.
"Where is my ox?" etc.
He said to someone in the market, etc.
He said to a guard, etc.
"Where is my ox?"

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: ״אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה אַתָּה סָח״ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: He said to him: "I don't know what you are talking about," etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: וְכוּלָּן פְּטוּרִין מִשְּׁבוּעַת שׁוֹמְרִין,
phrases.english: Rav said: All of them are exempt from the oath of guards,
but they are liable because of an oath of utterance.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אַף פְּטוּרִין מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּעַת בִּיטּוּי.
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: They are also exempt from an oath of utterance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: וְכוּלָּן פְּטוּרִין מִשְּׁבוּעַת שׁוֹמְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It returns to new cases in the משנה after the discussion of the four kinds of guards.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: exempt from שבועת שומרים but liable for שבועת ביטוי. שמואל: exempt from both.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רב and שמואל disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea is behind the argument between רב and שמואל. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody is attacking either opinion here. The גמרא simply wants to find the basic rule that each one holds, so the argument makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? A question asking for the root of an argument

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the argument just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that separates רב from שמואל.

steps.title: Future oath versus yes-or-no oath
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds that a שבועת ביטוי must be an oath that could also be said about the future, and this one cannot. רב holds it is enough that it can be said as a yes or a no.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds: this oath cannot be said about the future. רב holds: it can be said as a 'no' and as a 'yes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument is about what kind of oath counts as a שבועת ביטוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says only an oath that someone could also make about the future counts as a שבועת ביטוי. An oath about what happened to the ox cannot be made about the future, so there is no קרבן. רב says it is enough that the oath can be said either way ('it was stolen' or 'it was not stolen'), so there is a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: About the future
A 'no' and a 'yes', an oath that can be said in the negative or the positive
Holds, is of the opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב and שמואל are arguing about guards here. Their argument is about the general rule of which oaths count as a שבועת ביטוי. The guard cases are just one place it comes up.

phrases.english: Shmuel holds: It cannot be said about the future.
phrases.notes: He means: you couldn't swear this kind of oath about what will happen, so it doesn't count as an oath of utterance.

phrases.english: And Rav holds: It can be said as a 'no' and a 'yes.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל: a שבועת ביטוי must be possible about the future. רב: it is enough that it can be said as a no or a yes.

steps.title: They already argued this about the stone in the sea
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רב and שמואל already argued about this same principle with an oath that someone threw a stone into the sea, so why repeat it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But they already argued about this once! As it was said: 'I swear that so-and-so threw a stone into the sea,' or 'I swear he did not throw it.' רב said: liable. שמואל said: exempt. רב says liable because it can be said as a no or a yes, and שמואל says exempt because it cannot be said about the future!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need this argument here, since רב and שמואל already argued about the exact same idea in another case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the stone case, someone swears about what another person did. That oath can be said as yes or no, but it can't be said about the future, since he can't control what someone else does. Since the same principle already shows up there, this second argument seems repeated for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, an opening word for a challenge
They argued
One time, on another occasion
A stone, a pebble

phrases.english: But they already argued about this one time,
as it was said: "I swear that so-and-so threw a stone into the sea,"
or "I swear that he did not throw it":
Rav said: He is liable,
and Shmuel said: He is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר חַיָּיב – דְּאִיתַהּ בְּלָאו וְהֵן,
phrases.english: Rav says liable, because it can be said as a 'no' and a 'yes,'
and Shmuel says exempt, because it cannot be said about the future!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason given in step 18 to argue that the argument of step 16 is repeated.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to state the argument of רב and שמואל about the guard cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same principle (yes-or-no versus future) is already the basis of their argument in the stone case, so stating it again here seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Both cases are needed: an oath given by the court is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both arguments are needed. In the stone case the person swore on his own. In the guard case the בית דין gave the oath, and we might have thought רב agrees with שמואל because of רבי אמי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. If we had only been taught the stone case, we would say רב holds liable only there, because he swore on his own. But here, where the court makes him swear, I would say רב agrees with שמואל, like רבי אמי. As רבי אמי said: any oath the judges make a person swear does not make him liable for a שבועת ביטוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the argument has to be stated in the guard case too. Without it, we might have thought רב agrees here that there is no קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a real difference between the cases: in the stone case the man chose to swear, while the guard swore because the בית דין told him to. רבי אמי says a court-given oath never makes someone liable for a שבועת ביטוי. So stating the argument here teaches that רב says liable even for an oath the court gave.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed, both statements are necessary
On his own, by his own choice
The court, בית דין
Agrees, admits
Judges

steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל argue whether a שבועת ביטוי must be possible about the future. Their argument appears twice: once for an oath someone makes on his own (the stone), and once for an oath the court gives (the guard). This shows that רב holds liable even against the idea of רבי אמי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that, according to רב, an oath given by the בית דין can still bring a קרבן for a false שבועת ביטוי, unlike רבי אמי's general rule.

phrases.english: It is needed;
because if we had only been taught this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the stone in the sea.

phrases.english: only in this case does Rav say liable,
because he is swearing on his own;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָךְ, דְּבֵי דִינָא מַשְׁבְּעִי לֵיהּ –
phrases.english: but in that case, where the court makes him swear,
phrases.notes: 'That case' is the guard in our משנה.

phrases.english: I would say he agrees with Shmuel,
like Rabbi Ami;
as Rabbi Ami said:
Any oath that the judges make a person swear,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּעַת בִּיטּוּי.
phrases.english: one is not liable for it as an oath of utterance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא (showing that both statements are needed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the guard's oath was given by the בית דין, רב might agree with שמואל, following רבי אמי, that there is no liability for שבועת ביטוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב holds liable even when the court gives the oath, so the argument had to be stated in the guard case too.

steps.title: The second half of why both cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: If the argument had been stated only in the guard case, we might think שמואל agrees with רב in the stone case. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the argument had been stated only in this case (the guard who swore in בית דין), we would say that only here שמואל says he is exempt. But in that other case (the stone thrown into the sea), say that שמואל agrees with רב. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from step 20. It shows that the guard case alone would not have taught us the stone case either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 showed that the stone case alone could have misled us about רב's view. Now the גמרא shows the reverse: from the guard case alone, we might think שמואל exempts only because בית דין gave the oath. Then we would wrongly think he agrees with רב when a person swears by himself. Each case teaches something the other cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. The גמרא's word for 'both statements are needed.'
I might say. It introduces a possible wrong conclusion.
Agrees, concedes.

steps.whatToRemember: The argument appears twice because each case could mislead us alone. From the stone case, we might think רב agrees with שמואל when בית דין gives the oath. From the guard case, we might think שמואל agrees with רב when a person swears by himself.

phrases.english: And if it had been stated only in this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the guard who swore in בית דין, the case we're discussing right now.

phrases.english: I would say it is in this case that שמואל says he is exempt,
but in that other case
phrases.notes: 'That other case' is the oath that someone threw a stone into the sea.

phrases.english: say that he agrees with רב;
so both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided answer begun in step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the guard case, we would think שמואל exempts only because בית דין gave the oath. Then he would agree with רב when a person swears by himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases must be stated so that we know each opinion holds in both kinds of oath.

steps.title: רבי אמי: an oath given by judges is not a שבועת ביטוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now looks at רבי אמי's rule, which was mentioned in step 20. Any oath that judges make a person take is not counted as a שבועת ביטוי. The פסוק speaks of someone who swears by himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רבי אמי said: any oath that the judges make a person take is not treated as a שבועת ביטוי. The פסוק says, 'Or a person who swears, speaking with his lips,' which means one who swears on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: Since step 20 mentioned רבי אמי's rule, the גמרא now quotes it in full. It also gives the פסוק it comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי holds that the punishment for a false שבועת ביטוי applies only when a person chooses to swear. If judges make him swear, it falls outside this category. He learns this from the פסוק, which describes a person who swears with his own lips.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא goes back to look at a statement it quoted only in passing.
Judges
An oath of speech: a person swears about something he will do or did. A false one brings a קרבן.
On his own, by his own choice

phrases.english: The matter itself:
רבי אמי said:
Any oath that the judges make a person take
is not treated as a שבועת ביטוי;
as it says:
'Or a person, if he swears,'
'speaking out with his lips' —
meaning on his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the rule that step 20 used as the possible reason רב might agree with שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An oath that judges give a person is not a שבועת ביטוי. Only an oath a person takes on his own is.

steps.title: How the word כי shows the oath must be self-chosen
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי's reading follows ריש לקיש, who says the word כי has four meanings. Here it means 'if': if a person swears on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows ריש לקיש, who said: the word כי is used in four ways: 'if,' 'perhaps,' 'rather,' and 'because.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי אמי got the idea of 'on his own' from the פסוק. It brings ריש לקיש's rule about the word כי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on the word כי in the פסוק. ריש לקיש says this word can mean 'if.' Read that way, the פסוק says: 'if a person swears.' That describes a person who decides by himself to swear, not one who is ordered to by בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: A word with several meanings. Here it means 'if.'
Four meanings, four uses of a word
Perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read כי here as 'because' or 'that.' The whole proof depends on reading it as 'if,' which describes a person who chooses to swear.

phrases.english: This follows ריש לקיש,
for ריש לקיש said:
The word כי is used with four meanings:
'if,' 'perhaps,' 'rather,' and 'because.'
phrases.notes: In our פסוק, the meaning used is the first one, 'if.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how step 22 learns 'on his own' from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's reading that the פסוק speaks only of a self-chosen oath
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's rule that כי can mean 'if'

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the guards are liable for שבועת ביטוי, with some exceptions
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that all the guards whom the משנה exempts from the guard-oath penalty are still liable for שבועת ביטוי. There are two exceptions. One is a borrower who says 'I don't know what you're talking about.' The other is a paid guard or renter whose ox was really stolen or lost, but who claimed an אונס. Those are liable for the guard oath itself, because they denied money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: all of them are exempt from the guard oath but liable for a שבועת ביטוי. There are two exceptions. One is a borrower who says 'I don't know what you are talking about.' The other is a case of theft or loss with a paid guard or renter, where the ox was really stolen or lost and he swore to something else. Those are liable, because they denied money that they owed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר's ruling about all the guard cases of the משנה. It is the final ruling of the פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that the false oaths in the משנה still count as שבועת ביטוי even though בית דין gave them. That fits רב's view, not שמואל's. The exceptions are cases where the false oath really freed the guard from paying. There, the false oath denied money, so it counts as a full guard oath.

keyTerms.meaning: The guard oath: an oath a guard takes in בית דין about an item left with him
A borrower. He pays even if the item was stolen or lost.
A paid guard. He pays if the item was stolen or lost.
A renter
He denied him money. His false oath freed him from paying what he owed.

steps.whatToRemember: A false guard oath brings the guard-oath penalty only when it really denies money that the guard would have had to pay. In the other cases the oath is still a שבועת ביטוי, which follows רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sums up the rule of the whole פרק: a false claim that would not free the guard from paying is not a punishable guard oath.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר says:
All of them are exempt from the guard oath
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the guards whom the משנה called exempt.

phrases.english: but liable for a שבועת ביטוי;

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מֵ״אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה אַתָּה סָח״ דְּשׁוֹאֵל,
phrases.english: except for a borrower who says 'I don't know what you are talking about,'
and theft or loss
phrases.notes: He means the ox was really stolen or lost, but the guard swore it died or was captured, like the case in step 4.

phrases.english: by a paid guard or by a renter,
where he is liable,
phrases.notes: Here 'liable' means liable for the guard oath itself, not for a שבועת ביטוי.

phrases.english: because he denied him money.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר כּוּלָּן פְּטוּרִין מִשְּׁבוּעַת שׁוֹמְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the רב–שמואל argument from step 16 and gives a ruling that matches רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The guards in the משנה are exempt from the guard oath but liable for שבועת ביטוי. A borrower who says 'I don't know' is liable for the guard oath, since he denied money. So is a paid guard or renter whose ox was really stolen or lost, when he swore to an אונס.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing ארבעה שומרין and מסכת שבועות
steps.stepSummary: The closing words for the פרק ארבעה שומרין and for the whole of מסכת שבועות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק ארבעה שומרין, and מסכת שבועות is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line for the end of a פרק. Here it also marks the end of the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the legal discussion. It shows a wish to come back and learn this פרק again. Here it also announces that מסכת שבועות is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. Said at the end of a פרק.
It is finished, completed

phrases.english: We will return to you, ארבעה שומרין,
and מסכת שבועות is finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek and the מסכת after רבי אלעזר's final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק ארבעה שומרין and מסכת שבועות are complete.
